- If sentiment is bullish (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤-0.5) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in adjusting downward; delay correction until 2–3 days after sentiment flip.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to next forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish spikes followed by corrections, model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in subsequent periods.
